title: The Evening Brief: CFTC rulemaking clears first hurdle; market sentiment tilts greedier
dek: The CFTC filed a crypto market structure rulemaking with the White House on September 17, moving forward unilaterally after Congress rejected the CLARITY Act two days earlier. Regulatory risk is now centered on October 1, when the White House review window closes.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: October 1 marks the end of the White House's initial 10 working day review of the CFTC's crypto rulemaking. What happens at that deadline, publication, extension, or reconsideration, will signal whether the executive branch intends to let the CFTC write crypto rules independently.
bottom_line: The CFTC moved to White House review on September 17, signaling intent to write crypto market structure rules via executive authority after the Senate rejected legislation. October 1 marks the threshold: what the White House does when OIRA's review window closes will show whether the executive branch intends to let independent agencies write crypto rules unilaterally or coordinate a centralized approach.
body: Regulation moved decisively this week after Congress stalled. The CFTC sent a crypto market structure rulemaking (RIN 3038-AF80) to the White House Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs on September 17, two days after the Senate rejected the CLARITY Act in a 49-50 vote. The filing entered OIRA review at the prerule stage, a preliminary step that precedes formal proposed-rule publication. As the desk reported, CFTC Chairman Selig directed staff in January to draft rules on retail leveraged crypto trading, designated contract market requirements tailored to crypto, and eligible tokenized collateral, work now formally in the executive review pipeline. The agency's Market Participants Division also issued a no-action letter the same day on passive trading software, signaling a regulatory approach designed to build legal channels for innovation rather than block market participants.

EU and traditional-finance sectors moved on parallel tracks. The European Commission's staking review consultation, open until September 30, is asking whether liquid staking services (now at $44 billion globally, with Ethereum representing nearly 80% of that) should face dedicated regulatory requirements separate from MiCA's custody rules. The question reflects growing policymaker concern about withdrawal delays, slashing risk, and leverage created when staking-yield tokens move through DeFi. On the asset-tokenization front, Coinbase's tokenized stocks (NVDAc, AAPLc, GOOGLc, METAc) crossed $1 billion in 30-day rolling DEX volume by September 19, an 830.5% jump from August's $228 million. The product is restricted to non-US traders, positioning traditional-asset derivatives as a new layer of cross-border market structure that regulators will eventually have to address. Hyperliquid's decentralized perpetuals platform surpassed $8.1 billion in open interest on September 20, a new all-time high commanding 10.9% of global perpetual futures volume, driven in part by tokenized real-world asset markets that now sometimes represent more than 30% of platform volume.

Market sentiment moved into greed territory despite technical warning signs. The desk's Fear & Greed Index stood at 71 on the 19th, up from the 50-74 range of the prior 30 days, reflecting confidence in crypto's near-term direction. Bitcoin traded at $81,222.17 on the 19th, up 0.4% on the day and 25.2% over the month, though still 34.9% below its 12-month high of $124,739.81. Ethereum moved up 0.7% on the day and 37.5% for the month at $2,630.74. Per the desk's leverage board at OKX, BTC funding rates annualized at 10.5%, and SOL at 11.0%, signaling sustained long positioning. However, the RSI on both BTC and ETH sat elevated at 64.2 and 65.4 respectively, and MACD signals remained below their signal lines on both assets, a technical divergence in a greed environment. The week ending September 20 saw $653 million in bitcoin move onto exchanges, the third straight week of net inflows to exchange wallets, per the desk's Whale Watch board, a pattern that typically precedes liquidation events or profit-taking. Stablecoin reserves remain flat, up just 0.68% over the month at $310 billion.

The tape reflects mixed positioning. Per the desk's ETF flows board, bitcoin saw an inflow of $433 million on September 18, but the five-session window shows only $6.1 million net inflow over that span, indicating the latest daily print is an outlier, not a sustained trend. Ethereum saw a $143.7 million inflow on the same day, but the five-session window shows a net outflow of $140.6 million, a sharp disagreement that signals institutional rotation out of ether into bitcoin or stable assets.

Regulatory checkpoints now telescope into October. The White House OIRA review of the CFTC rulemaking closes on October 1 unless the White House requests reconsideration or extension, which it may do for up to 30 days. The SEC's Regulation Crypto Assets proposal remains in the Federal Register with comments open until October 20. The EU's MiCA staking consultation closes September 30 at 23:59 CEST. If the CFTC publishes a proposed rule on or shortly after October 1, the agency will have signaled that the White House poses no significant friction to unilateral rulemaking post-Supreme Court Humphrey's Executor reversal. If the deadline passes with extension or reconsideration, it will indicate the White House is coordinating with or applying pressure to the CFTC to align with the SEC's own custody and Regulation Crypto Assets agenda, or waiting for congressional activity. Thailand's stablecoin travel rule comments are due September 25.
